title: TSMC’s 2-Nanometer Outpaces 3-Nanometer Growth
gist: Supply-chain sources say TSMC will lift monthly 2-nanometer capacity from 90,000 wafers at end-2026 to 110,000 by mid-2027 (+22%) while 3-nanometer goes from over 180,000 to 210,000 (+16%), against 2026 capital expenditure of $60–64 billion with 70–80% aimed at advanced processes. Simultaneous expansion of both leading nodes — plus new 3nm sites in Taiwan, Arizona and Japan and conversion of some Taiwanese 5nm equipment — signals customer conviction that AI infrastructure and premium processor demand holds.

insights.claim: TSMC's monthly 2-nanometer capacity is targeted to rise from 90,000 wafers at the end of 2026 to 110,000 by mid-2027, a 22% increase in roughly six months.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Sets the hard supply ceiling for leading-edge AI and flagship mobile silicon through mid-2027 — allocation, not demand, will determine who ships.
insights.quote: monthly 2-nanometer capacity is targeted to rise from 90,000 wafers at the end of 2026 to 110,000 by mid-2027, a 22% increase

insights.claim: TSMC's 3-nanometer monthly capacity is expected to grow from more than 180,000 wafers at end-2026 to 210,000 by mid-2027, an increase exceeding 16%.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The mature leading-edge node keeps expanding rather than rolling off — good for equipment order continuity and for customers on N3 long after N2 launches.
insights.quote: Three-nanometer capacity is expected to grow from more than 180,000 wafers to 210,000 over the same period, an increase exceeding 16%.

insights.claim: Although the 2nm percentage increase is larger, 3nm adds roughly 30,000 wafers per month of absolute capacity versus about 20,000 for 2nm, so the older node still absorbs more incremental tooling and output.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Headline growth rates mislead on equipment spend and wafer revenue mix — N3 remains the bigger absolute capacity story into mid-2027.

insights.claim: TSMC's 3-nanometer platform reportedly stood at just 120,000 to 130,000 monthly wafers at the end of 2025, meaning the node will have roughly doubled its capacity within eighteen months.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Quantifies the steepest leading-edge ramp on record — a template for how fast N2 could scale if AI demand persists.
insights.quote: whose monthly capacity reportedly stood at 120,000 to 130,000 wafers at the end of 2025
insights.locator: The expansion would extend the rapid scaling of TSMC’s 3-nanometer platform

insights.claim: Even though 2-nanometer has become TSMC's most advanced production node, sustained customer demand keeps 3-nanometer manufacturing commercially important rather than obsolete.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Node lifecycles are lengthening — the depreciation and pricing model for N-1 nodes is better than the classic cadence assumes.
insights.quote: sustained customer demand means 3-nanometer manufacturing remains commercially important
insights.locator: Although 2-nanometer technology has now become the company’s most advanced production node

insights.claim: TSMC expects 2026 capital expenditure of $60 billion to $64 billion, with roughly 70% to 80% of it directed toward advanced processes.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Roughly $42–51bn of advanced-node capex sets the revenue pool for ASML, Applied Materials, Lam and Tokyo Electron — the single largest swing factor in WFE.
insights.quote: The chipmaker expects 2026 capital expenditure of $60 billion to $64 billion, with roughly 70% to 80% directed toward advanced processes.
insights.locator: Nevertheless, the plans are consistent with its enormous investment program

insights.claim: TSMC is adding 3-nanometer facilities in Taiwan, Arizona and Japan while converting some of its Taiwanese 5-nanometer equipment to 3nm.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Multi-geography N3 build plus 5nm conversion means part of the capacity increase comes from reuse, lowering the implied greenfield capex per incremental wafer.
insights.quote: It is adding 3-nanometer facilities in Taiwan, Arizona and Japan while converting some Taiwanese 5-nanometer equipment.
insights.locator: Nevertheless, the plans are consistent with its enormous investment program

insights.claim: Converting existing 5-nanometer equipment to 3-nanometer implies 5nm demand is soft enough to cannibalise, even as both leading nodes expand.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A warning that the boom is concentrated at the bleeding edge — N5-and-older utilisation is the soft spot to monitor for broader demand health.
insights.locator: It is adding 3-nanometer facilities in Taiwan, Arizona and Japan

insights.claim: TSMC has not confirmed the reported capacity targets and says capacity information should come from official company announcements.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: These are supply-chain-sourced numbers, not guidance — size positions accordingly until the next earnings call confirms.
insights.quote: TSMC has not confirmed the reported targets, saying capacity information should come from official company announcements.
insights.locator: TSMC has not confirmed the reported targets

themes.theme: Capacity plans as a demand signal

insights.claim: TSMC's capacity decisions function as a leading indicator of future industry demand because it manufactures the world's most sophisticated chips for many leading technology companies.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Use TSMC wafer-start plans as a forward read on hyperscaler and smartphone orders that customers themselves have not yet disclosed.
insights.quote: making its capacity decisions a key indicator of future industry demand

insights.claim: Expanding both 2nm and 3nm simultaneously suggests customers expect AI infrastructure spending and demand for premium processors to remain strong rather than plateau.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Dual-node expansion is a stronger demand signal than a single-node ramp — customers are committing to volume on both platforms at once.
insights.quote: Expanding both nodes suggests customers expect AI infrastructure spending and demand for premium processors to remain strong.

insights.claim: Demand is being driven jointly by artificial intelligence, smartphones and high-performance computing, not by AI alone, at the leading edge.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: A broader demand base at N2/N3 than the pure-AI narrative implies, which cushions leading-edge utilisation if AI capex pauses.
insights.quote: underscoring the strength of demand for the technologies powering artificial intelligence, smartphones and high-performance computing
insights.locator: TSMC is preparing another major increase in leading-edge chip production

insights.claim: The expansion raises execution risk because new fabs and advanced lithography require immense spending, high yields and dependable equipment supply simultaneously.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Yield ramp and EUV tool delivery are the two failure modes that would turn record capex into margin compression — watch gross margin guidance.
insights.quote: It also raises execution risks: new fabs and advanced lithography require immense spending, high yields and dependable equipment supply.
insights.locator: More capacity could ease supply constraints

insights.claim: More capacity could ease supply constraints, support faster product launches for customers, and drive TSMC revenue to another record.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Relief in leading-edge allocation would let downstream fabless customers accelerate launches — a second-order positive for AI system builders.
insights.locator: More capacity could ease supply constraints

insights.claim: Successfully executing the dual-node ramp would strengthen TSMC's technological lead, pricing power and strategic importance while reinforcing Taiwan's central role in the global semiconductor ecosystem.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: Concentration risk cuts both ways: it deepens TSMC's moat and pricing leverage while raising the geopolitical stakes attached to Taiwan.
insights.quote: Success would strengthen TSMC’s technological lead, pricing power and strategic importance, while reinforcing Taiwan’s central role in the global semiconductor ecosystem.
insights.locator: More capacity could ease supply constraints

insights.claim: Following through on these targets would signal confidence that leading-edge chip demand can justify historic investment levels for years to come, not just for a single cycle.
insights.speaker: Daniel Nenni
insights.so_what: The multi-year framing is the bull case for the whole equipment and materials chain; a target cut would be the clearest cycle-top tell.
insights.quote: It would also signal confidence that leading-edge chip demand can justify historic investment levels for years to come.
insights.locator: More capacity could ease supply constraints
